canonical.title: Morris Inorder Traversal (O(1) Space)
canonical.sourceFilePath: 11. Binary Trees/3. Hard/12. Morris Inorder Traversal.cpp

narrative.title: The Thread-Backed Shelf Reconciliation
narrative.scenario: An inventory drone must list every shelf of a tree-layout aisle in left-to-right order while forbidden from carrying a routing table. Its trick: whenever it steps into a left branch, it first strings a temporary return-thread from that branch's rightmost shelf up to the current junction. The thread tells it when the branch is exhausted; it snips the thread on the way out, restoring the aisle byte for byte.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child).
narrative.outputFormat: Return the node values in inorder (left subtree, root, right subtree).
constraints: Expected extra space: O(1) — Morris threading, no stack or queue

testCases.explanation: The left wing reads 4-2-5, then the root 1, then 3 with its right child 6.
The root has no left subtree, so 1 leads; node 2's left child 3 precedes it.

hintLevels: Level 1: Inorder means 'finish the left, then log me' — you need a cheap way to know when a left walk is done.
Level 2: Thread the left subtree's rightmost node back to the current root; arriving via the thread means the left is complete.
Level 3: Record the value when the thread already exists (or there is no left child), then cut the thread and step right.
